accepted.s: The Technology Mission on Oilseeds, launched in 1986, was associated with which of the following developments?
o: Promotion of oilseeds, with pulses and maize added later, under the Yellow Revolution
Promotion of rice-based systems in eastern India under the White Revolution
Promotion of millets exclusively for industrial use
Promotion of sugarcane and cotton under the Blue Revolution
accepted.x: The Technology Mission on Oilseeds was launched in 1986. It focused on oilseeds, with pulses and maize added later, and was associated with the Yellow Revolution led by Sam Pitroda.
accepted.tq: Match the mission with its launch year, target crops and associated revolution.
accepted.sec: Crop missions → target crops (NFSM, BGREI, INSIMP, oilseeds mission)  [APPSC, GROUP-II]

accepted.s: Which one of the following is correctly matched?
o: BGREI — Rice-based systems in eastern States
accepted.x: BGREI is a sub-scheme of RKVY concerned with rice-based systems in the eastern States. INSIMP concerns millets, NMOOP concerns oilseeds and oil palm, and NFSM has a broader crop portfolio.
accepted.tq: Use the mission-target association to eliminate swapped crop objectives.
accepted.sec: Crop missions → target crops (NFSM, BGREI, INSIMP, oilseeds mission)  [APPSC, GROUP-II]

accepted.s: The Bringing Green Revolution to Eastern India (BGREI) programme covers which of the following groups of States?
o: Assam, Bihar, Chhattisgarh, Jharkhand, Odisha, eastern Uttar Pradesh and West Bengal
Kerala, Tamil Nadu, Telangana, Andhra Pradesh and Goa
Madhya Pradesh, Rajasthan, Gujarat, Maharashtra and Chhattisgarh בלבד
Punjab, Haryana, Rajasthan, Gujarat, Maharashtra and Karnataka
accepted.x: BGREI covers rice-based systems in Assam, Bihar, Chhattisgarh, Jharkhand, Odisha, eastern Uttar Pradesh and West Bengal.
accepted.tq: Test the complete geographical membership of a named programme.
accepted.sec: Crop missions → target crops (NFSM, BGREI, INSIMP, oilseeds mission)  [APPSC, GROUP-II]

accepted.s: INSIMP, a scheme under the Rashtriya Krishi Vikas Yojana, was primarily associated with which crop group?
accepted.x: INSIMP was launched under RKVY for millets, with the objective of promoting nutritional security.
accepted.tq: Distinguish similar crop missions by their precise target crop.
accepted.sec: Crop missions → target crops (NFSM, BGREI, INSIMP, oilseeds mission)  [APPSC, GROUP-II]

accepted.s:
Arrange the following missions in chronological order of their launch:
A. NMOOP
B. Technology Mission on Oilseeds
C. INSIMP
D. NFSM
accepted.x: The Technology Mission on Oilseeds was launched in 1986, NFSM in 2007-08, INSIMP in 2011-12 and NMOOP in 2014.
accepted.tq: Place the missions by their launch years before comparing the options.
accepted.sec: Crop missions → target crops (NFSM, BGREI, INSIMP, oilseeds mission)  [APPSC, GROUP-II]

accepted.s:
Which of the following statements regarding the oilseed-related missions is correct?
1. NMOOP was launched in 2014 for oilseeds and oil palm.
2. NMEO-Oil Palm was launched in 2021.
3. NMEO-Oilseeds was launched in 2024 with an approximate target of 70 million tonnes by 2030-31.
Select the correct answer using the code given below.
accepted.x: All three statements are correct: NMOOP dates from 2014, NMEO-Oil Palm from 2021, and NMEO-Oilseeds from 2024 with a target of about 70 MT by 2030-31.
accepted.tq: Verify each mission by its year, crop focus and quantitative target.
accepted.sec: Crop missions → target crops (NFSM, BGREI, INSIMP, oilseeds mission)  [APPSC, GROUP-II]

accepted.s: The ‘Tilhan Mission’, referred to in February 2020, relates primarily to which of the following?
accepted.x: The Tilhan Mission relates to oilseed production.
accepted.tq: Discriminate between similarly named crop initiatives by identifying the target crop.
accepted.sec: Crop missions → target crops (NFSM, BGREI, INSIMP, oilseeds mission)  [APPSC, GROUP-II]

accepted.s: The Mission for Aatmanirbharta in Pulses, covering 2025-2031, primarily targets which combination of pulses?
accepted.x: The mission targets tur, urad and masur and seeks to end pulse imports.
accepted.tq: Test the exact membership of a named crop group rather than its broad objective.
accepted.sec: Crop missions → target crops (NFSM, BGREI, INSIMP, oilseeds mission)  [APPSC, GROUP-II]

accepted.s: The first major regional concentration of the Green Revolution was observed mainly in which area?
o: Kerala, Tamil Nadu and coastal Karnataka
Assam, Odisha and eastern West Bengal
Punjab, Haryana and western Uttar Pradesh
accepted.x: The first phase was concentrated in Punjab, Haryana and western Uttar Pradesh, while several eastern and rainfed regions lagged.
accepted.tq: Identify the initial regional core instead of the later expansion area.
accepted.sec: Green Revolution outcomes - crops and regions benefited, regional disparity  [APPSC, GROUP-II]

accepted.s:
Consider the following statements about the regional spread of the Green Revolution:
1. Irrigated rice deltas of Andhra Pradesh and Tamil Nadu benefited through irrigation.
2. Madhya Pradesh, Bihar, Odisha, West Bengal and Assam lagged during the first phase.
3. During the second phase in the 1980s, the spread extended towards both eastern and western regions.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
accepted.x: All three statements correctly describe the regional pattern: irrigated rice deltas benefited, the eastern belt initially lagged, and the second phase spread eastward and westward in the 1980s.
accepted.tq: Combine regional beneficiaries, lagging regions and the later phase of expansion.
accepted.sec: Green Revolution outcomes - crops and regions benefited, regional disparity  [APPSC, GROUP-II]

accepted.s: The growth rate of agricultural output during the second phase of the Green Revolution was approximately how much, compared with 2.3% in the earlier phase?
accepted.x: Output growth rose to approximately 3.4% during the second phase, compared with 2.3% earlier.
accepted.tq: Use the comparative numerical value rather than the familiar earlier figure.
accepted.sec: Green Revolution outcomes - crops and regions benefited, regional disparity  [APPSC, GROUP-II]

accepted.s: Which of the following groups was comparatively neglected by the Green Revolution?
o: Large farmers with more than 10 hectares in irrigated areas
Rice farmers in irrigated deltas of Andhra Pradesh
Wheat farmers in Punjab and Haryana
Pulses, oilseeds and millets in rainfed and hilly areas
accepted.x: The gains were captured disproportionately by farmers with more than 10 hectares, while rainfed and hilly areas and crops such as pulses, oilseeds and millets were neglected.
accepted.tq: Find the option that reverses the documented beneficiaries and neglected groups.
accepted.sec: Green Revolution outcomes - crops and regions benefited, regional disparity  [APPSC, GROUP-II]

accepted.s: The N:P:K ratio in Indian agriculture has worsened to which of the following, compared with the ideal ratio of 4:2:1?
accepted.x: The prevailing N:P:K ratio is given as 10.9:4.1:1, whereas the ideal ratio is 4:2:1. This imbalance is associated with concerns such as groundwater depletion and salinity.
accepted.tq: Separate the actual input ratio from the ideal benchmark.
accepted.sec: Green Revolution outcomes - crops and regions benefited, regional disparity  [APPSC, GROUP-II]

accepted.s: Which phase of agricultural development is marked by a price policy based on minimum support price and procurement?
accepted.x: The third phase of agricultural development is marked by a price policy based on MSP and procurement.
accepted.tq: Associate the policy characteristic with the correct phase of agricultural development.
accepted.sec: Green Revolution outcomes - crops and regions benefited, regional disparity  [APPSC, GROUP-II]

accepted.s: The National Commission on Agriculture was set up in which year, and when did it submit its final report?
accepted.x: The National Commission on Agriculture was set up in 1970 and submitted its final report in 1976.
accepted.tq: Pair the establishment year with the report year instead of treating them as one date.
accepted.sec: Employment potential by crop group (National Commission on Agriculture)  [APPSC, GROUP-II]

accepted.s: The committee constituted to examine the objective of doubling farmers’ income was chaired by whom?
accepted.x: The committee on doubling farmers’ income was chaired by Ashok Dalwai. It was set up in 2016 and submitted its report in 2018.
accepted.tq: Match the committee’s objective with its chairman rather than with another agricultural expert.
accepted.sec: Doubling Farmers' Income committee → chairman  [GROUP-II]

accepted.s:
Consider the following statements about the committee on doubling farmers’ income:
1. It was set up in 2016.
2. It submitted its report in 2018.
3. It was chaired by Ashok Dalwai.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
accepted.x: The Ashok Dalwai Committee was set up in 2016, submitted its report in 2018 and was chaired by Ashok Dalwai.
accepted.tq: Cross-check the committee through its year of constitution, report year and chairmanship.
accepted.sec: Doubling Farmers' Income committee → chairman  [GROUP-II]

accepted.s: Which of the following pairs correctly represents the recorded 2025-26 output figures?
o: Foodgrains: 354.70 million tonnes; horticulture: 377.78 million tonnes
Foodgrains: 376.56 million tonnes; horticulture: 377.78 million tonnes
Foodgrains: 377.78 million tonnes; horticulture: 376.56 million tonnes
Foodgrains: 376.56 million tonnes; horticulture: 354.70 million tonnes
accepted.x: The recorded 2025-26 figures are 376.56 million tonnes of foodgrains and 377.78 million tonnes of horticulture output.
accepted.tq: Read the paired figures carefully and avoid reversing the two sectors.
accepted.sec: Universal angles

accepted.s: Which of the following statements correctly describes the recent agricultural export position mentioned in relation to 2025-26?
o: Agricultural exports reached 45.70 billion dollars, alongside an oilseed crisis.
Agricultural exports reached 70.54 billion dollars, alongside a rice crisis.
Agricultural exports fell to 54.70 billion dollars because of a wheat crisis.
Agricultural exports reached 54.70 billion dollars, alongside a cotton crisis.
accepted.x: Agricultural exports reached 54.70 billion dollars, while the sector simultaneously faced a cotton crisis.
accepted.tq: Link the exact export value with the associated sectoral concern.
accepted.sec: Universal angles

accepted.s: Which one of the following best describes the agricultural situation in Andhra Pradesh?
o: Its paddy yield is about 10 tonnes per hectare and output remains constant each year.
Its paddy yield is below 2 tonnes per hectare and foodgrain output is independent of the monsoon.
Its paddy yield is about 6 tonnes per hectare, but foodgrain output fluctuates with the monsoon.
Its paddy cultivation is confined to rainfed uplands and has no major deltaic concentration.
accepted.x: Andhra Pradesh has a paddy yield of about 6 tonnes per hectare, among the best, but its foodgrain output fluctuates with monsoon conditions.
accepted.tq: Combine the State’s productivity strength with its monsoon-related vulnerability.
accepted.sec: Universal angles

accepted.s: The foodgrain output of Andhra Pradesh moved through which sequence during 2023-26?
accepted.x: The reported sequence of Andhra Pradesh foodgrain output was 143 lakh tonnes, followed by 162 lakh tonnes and 190 lakh tonnes across 2023-26.
accepted.tq: Arrange the successive annual output figures in their stated order.
accepted.sec: Universal angles

accepted.s: India’s rice yield, in comparison with China’s rice yield, is described as being:
accepted.x: India’s rice yield is described as less than half of China’s rice yield, highlighting a major yield gap.
accepted.tq: Focus on the direction and magnitude of the inter-country yield comparison.
accepted.sec: Universal angles

accepted.s: Which of the following statements best reflects the criticism concerning the sources of agricultural growth in India?
o: Growth has come more from expansion of area than from improvement in yield.
Growth has eliminated the yield gap with world averages.
Growth has come exclusively from yield improvement, with cultivated area declining continuously.
Growth has been driven only by foodgrain crops and not by allied activities.
accepted.x: A major criticism is that agricultural growth has depended more on area expansion than on yield improvement.
accepted.tq: Identify the cautious structural criticism and reject extreme formulations such as ‘exclusively’.
accepted.sec: Universal angles

accepted.s: The Indian Council of Agricultural Research released how many new climate-resilient or high-yield varieties, covering how many crops?
accepted.x: ICAR released 184 new climate-resilient or high-yield varieties covering 25 crops. Since 2014, 3,236 HYVs had been approved.
accepted.tq: Match the exact variety count with the number of crops covered.
accepted.sec: Universal angles

accepted.s: How many high-yielding varieties had been approved since 2014, according to the stated agricultural technology data?
accepted.x: A total of 3,236 high-yielding varieties had been approved since 2014.
accepted.tq: Distinguish the cumulative figure from the separate recent release of 184 varieties.
accepted.sec: Universal angles

accepted.s: Which of the following statements about Andhra Pradesh’s agricultural conditions is correct?
o: Foodgrain production was 116.86 lakh tonnes in 2024-25, while Kharif sowing reached 161% of normal.
Foodgrain production was 161.86 lakh tonnes in 2024-25, while Kharif 2026 sowing was about 61% of normal by 19 August because of El Nino.
Foodgrain production was 186.16 lakh tonnes in 2024-25, while Kharif sowing was about 91% of normal.
Foodgrain production was 161.86 lakh tonnes in 2024-25, while Kharif sowing was unaffected by El Nino.
accepted.x: Andhra Pradesh recorded 161.86 lakh tonnes of foodgrains in 2024-25. By 19 August 2026, Kharif sowing was only about 61% of normal, attributed to El Nino conditions.
accepted.tq: Combine a precise State-level output figure with a weather-related sowing constraint.
accepted.sec: Universal angles

accepted.s: Which sectoral pattern is identified as a recent feature of Indian agricultural growth?
o: Crop production alone is leading growth, while livestock and fisheries are contracting.
Livestock and fisheries are leading growth, while crop growth is about 3.5% and yields lag world averages.
Only horticulture is growing, with no contribution from livestock or fisheries.
Crop growth is about 8.5% and Indian yields exceed world averages.
accepted.x: Recent growth is led more by livestock and fisheries, while crop growth is about 3.5% and yields remain below world averages.
accepted.tq: Compare the leading subsectors with the weaker crop-growth and yield performance.
accepted.sec: Universal angles
